idiom_name: newtype implementing the target trait and forwarding to the inner value
implementation_notes: Rust has no reflection and no runtime proxies, so the interceptor is a newtype that implements the target trait, records the event and forwards the call to the inner value, with the audit sink shared behind an Arc because the wrapper cannot own a logger per call. The classic role structure is replaced by trait-based dispatch; the cost is that every trait method must be forwarded explicitly and default methods are inherited unaudited.
pitfalls: Every trait method must be forwarded by hand; default methods that are not overridden run unaudited with no warning.
The sink must be Send + Sync if the wrapper crosses threads.
Interception is static: the wrapper must be introduced at construction time, and code that keeps the concrete type instead of the trait cannot be audited retroactively.

variants.name: tower Service/Layer middleware
variants.idiom_name: tower::Service wrapper installed by a Layer
variants.implementation_notes: In async service stacks the interceptor is a tower service: a Layer wraps the inner Service, and the wrapper's Service::call records the attempt and returns an instrumented future that records the outcome when it resolves - the dispatcher is the executor itself. This is the idiomatic seam for hyper/axum/tonic-style code, but it only covers calls that travel through the service stack, and errors have to be observed through the future rather than around a call.
pitfalls: The audit record is complete only if the returned future is polled to completion - a dropped future (cancellation, timeouts) never records an outcome unless the wrapper handles drop.
poll_ready must be forwarded to the inner service unchanged, or backpressure and load-shedding behaviour silently change.
